chunks: From him, from Muhammad ibn Ali, from Ibn Mahbub, from Abd al-Aziz al-Abdi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)
regarding the Words of Allah, Mighty and Majestic:
Nay, it is clear verses in the chests of those who have been granted Knowledge
he said: 'They are the Imams (peace be upon them).'

key_terms.آيَاتٌ بَيِّنَاتٌ: Clear verses/manifest signs — the divine revelation preserved perfectly
key_terms.الْأَئِمَّةُ: The Imams — the twelve Imams of the Ahl al-Bayt who are the living vessels of Quranic knowledge
key_terms.الْعِلْمَ: Knowledge — in this context the divinely bestowed knowledge ('ilm ladunni) unique to the Imams
key_terms.صُدُورِ: Chests/hearts — in Islamic tradition, the seat of memory, intellect, and spiritual receptivity

ai.seo_question: Who are 'those who have been granted Knowledge' in Quran 29:49 according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: In this hadith, Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) provides an authoritative exegesis of Quran 29:49, which states that the Quran consists of 'clear verses in the chests of those who have been granted Knowledge.' The Imam identifies 'those who have been granted Knowledge' specifically as the Imams of the Ahl al-Bayt — those who carry the living knowledge of the Quran in their hearts. This is a foundational Shia theological statement establishing the unique epistemic authority of the Imams as the true custodians and interpreters of divine revelation.
